points.title: 贵族教育
points.description: 梅特涅出生于莱茵河畔的科布伦茨，这是一个重要的外交中心。他的父亲弗朗茨·乔治是奥地利驻莱茵邦联大使，母亲玛丽亚·贝娅特丽克斯是奥地利女大公的侍女。梅特涅从小接受严格的教育，学习多种语言，包括法语、英语、意大利语和拉丁语。这段经历培养了他对国际政治的早期认识，也塑造了他后来作为外交官的视野和思维方式。科布伦茨作为法国大革命时期流亡贵族的聚集地，使梅特涅从小目睹了革命对欧洲传统秩序的冲击，这深刻影响了他日后保守的政治理念。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Koblenz on the Rhine River, a significant diplomatic center, Metternich's father Franz George was the Austrian ambassador to the Rhine Confederation, and his mother Maria Beatrix was a lady-in-waiting to an Austrian archduchess. Metternich received a rigorous education, learning multiple languages including French, English, Italian, and Latin. This period shaped his early understanding of international politics and influenced his later career as a diplomat. As a gathering place for exiled nobles during the French Revolution, Koblenz allowed Metternich to witness firsthand the impact of revolution on traditional European order, profoundly influencing his later conservative political philosophy.

points.title: 外交崛起
points.description: 1795年，梅特涅进入奥地利外交部门，开始在维也纳的外交生涯。他迅速展现出卓越的外交才能，先后被派往柏林、圣彼得堡和巴黎等重要外交岗位。1806年，他被任命为驻巴黎大使，期间他密切观察拿破仑统治下的法国，并努力维护奥地利利益。1809年，梅特涅被召回维也纳，被任命为外交大臣。在担任外交大臣期间，他主导了1812年拿破仑入侵俄国时奥地利的立场，表面上保持中立，实际上暗中准备反法联盟。这一时期的外交历练使梅特涅成为欧洲政治舞台上不可忽视的人物，也为他日后主导维也纳会议奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1795, Metternich entered the Austrian diplomatic service, beginning his diplomatic career in Vienna. He quickly demonstrated exceptional diplomatic talent, serving in key posts in Berlin, St. Petersburg, and Paris. In 1806, he was appointed ambassador to Paris, where he closely observed Napoleon's France and worked to protect Austrian interests. Recalled to Vienna in 1809, he was appointed Foreign Minister. During his tenure, he guided Austria's position during Napoleon's 1812 invasion of Russia, maintaining a neutral stance while secretly preparing an anti-French coalition. This diplomatic experience established Metternich as a significant figure in European politics and laid the foundation for his later leadership at the Congress of Vienna.

points.title: 维也纳会议
points.description: 1814年至1815年的维也纳会议是梅特涅外交生涯的巅峰。作为奥地利代表团团长和会议的实际主导者之一，梅特涅成功协调了各国间的复杂利益冲突，重新塑造了拿破仑战争后的欧洲政治格局。他提出了'欧洲协调'理念，主张通过大国定期会议维持欧洲和平与稳定。会议期间，他促成了'神圣同盟'的建立，并主导了领土重新分配，如将波兰大部分领土划归俄国，普鲁士获得莱茵地区和萨克森部分领土，奥地利获得意大利北部和达尔马提亚。梅特涅的'均势外交'原则确保了欧洲近一个世纪的相对稳定，但也因压制民族主义和自由主义而受到批评。
points.descriptionEn: The Congress of Vienna from 1814 to 1815 marked the pinnacle of Metternich's diplomatic career. As head of the Austrian delegation and one of the meeting's actual leaders, he successfully mediated complex conflicts of interest among nations and reshaped Europe's political landscape after the Napoleonic Wars. He proposed the concept of 'European Concert,' advocating for regular great power conferences to maintain European peace and stability. During the congress, he facilitated the establishment of the Holy Alliance and led the territorial reallocation, such as assigning most of Poland to Russia, giving Prussia the Rhineland and parts of Saxony, and granting Austria northern Italy and Dalmatia. Metternich's 'balance of power' diplomacy ensured relative stability in Europe for nearly a century but was criticized for suppressing nationalism and liberalism.

points.title: 帝国首相
points.description: 1821年，梅特涅被任命为奥地利帝国首相兼外交大臣，成为奥地利实际上的统治者。在此期间，他推行保守主义政策，严格控制言论自由，镇压自由主义和民族主义运动。他建立了严密的警察监视系统，监控知识分子和政治活动家。梅特涅认为革命和民族主义是对欧洲稳定的主要威胁，因此他坚决反对任何形式的变革。1830年法国革命和1848年欧洲革命浪潮期间，梅特涅采取强硬措施维护奥地利统治，特别是在意大利和匈牙利地区。他的'梅特涅体系'成为欧洲保守主义的象征，但也积累了大量反对力量，最终在1848年革命中被推翻，被迫流亡。
points.descriptionEn: In 1821, Metternich was appointed Austrian Chancellor and Foreign Minister, becoming the de facto ruler of Austria. During this period, he implemented conservative policies, strictly controlling freedom of speech and suppressing liberal and nationalist movements. He established an extensive police surveillance system to monitor intellectuals and political activists. Metternich viewed revolution and nationalism as the primary threats to European stability, so he firmly opposed any form of change. During the 1830 French Revolution and the 1848 European revolutionary wave, Metternich took strong measures to maintain Austrian rule, particularly in Italy and Hungary. His 'Metternich System' became a symbol of European conservatism but accumulated significant opposition, ultimately leading to his overthrow during the 1848 revolutions and forcing him into exile.

points.title: 流亡岁月
points.description: 1848年革命爆发后，梅特涅被迫辞去所有职务，逃离维也纳，首先前往荷兰，后定居英国伦敦。在流亡期间，他继续关注欧洲政治发展，撰写回忆录和政治著作，为自己的政策辩护。尽管身处异国，他仍与奥地利宫廷保持联系，并通过书信影响奥地利政治。1849年，他的儿子理查德被任命为驻巴黎大使，这为梅特涅提供了间接影响法国政治的机会。流亡期间，梅特涅的健康状况逐渐恶化，但他依然保持着对政治的敏锐洞察力。1851年，奥地利皇帝弗朗茨一世去世后，新皇帝弗朗茨·约瑟夫一世允许梅特涅返回奥地利，但不再授予他政治职位。
points.descriptionEn: Following the outbreak of the 1848 revolutions, Metternich was forced to resign from all offices and flee Vienna, first to the Netherlands and then settling in London. During his exile, he continued to follow European political developments, writing memoirs and political works to defend his policies. Despite being abroad, he maintained contact with the Austrian court and influenced Austrian politics through correspondence. In 1849, his son Richard was appointed ambassador to Paris, providing Metternich with indirect opportunities to influence French politics. During exile, Metternich's health gradually declined, but he maintained his keen political insight. After Emperor Franz I's death in 1851, the new Emperor Franz Joseph I allowed Metternich to return to Austria but without granting him political positions.

points.title: 晚年岁月
points.description: 1851年返回维也纳后，梅特涅虽然不再担任正式政治职务，但仍保持着对政治的影响力，特别是通过与新皇帝弗朗茨·约瑟夫一世的私人关系。他在维也纳的府邸成为欧洲政治家的重要社交场所，许多重要政治人物仍向他寻求建议。梅特涅晚年致力于整理自己的政治文件和回忆录，试图为自己的政治遗产辩护。他继续关注欧洲政治发展，特别是克里米亚战争期间，他提出了恢复'欧洲协调'的建议。1859年，梅特涅在维也纳去世，享年86岁。他的葬礼成为奥地利帝国的重要事件，象征着一个时代的结束。梅特涅的去世标志着保守主义在欧洲政治中主导地位的终结，欧洲开始进入新的政治变革时期。
points.descriptionEn: After returning to Vienna in 1851, although no longer holding formal political positions, Metternich maintained political influence, particularly through his personal relationship with Emperor Franz Joseph I. His Vienna residence became an important social venue for European politicians, many of whom still sought his advice. In his later years, Metternich focused on organizing his political papers and memoirs, attempting to defend his political legacy. He continued to follow European political developments, particularly during the Crimean War, when he proposed reviving the 'European Concert.' Metternich died in Vienna in 1859 at the age of 86. His funeral became a significant event in the Austrian Empire, symbolizing the end of an era. Metternich's death marked the end of conservatism's dominant position in European politics, as Europe entered a new period of political transformation.

appraisal.zh: 梅特涅常被史学界视为19世纪欧洲最重要的外交家之一，他借「欧洲协调」与均势外交维系了欧洲近一个世纪的相对稳定，其理念被视为后来国际联盟与联合国的思想先驱，同时他也是旧秩序的坚定维护者。另一种看法认为，他压制民族自决与自由主义、以警察国家侵犯公民自由，1848年革命即表明其秩序难以为继，且过度依赖个人手腕，其体系在他下台后迅速瓦解。
appraisal.en: Metternich is generally regarded as one of 19th-century Europe's foremost diplomats, whose 'European Concert' and balance-of-power diplomacy sustained nearly a century of relative stability and prefigured later international organizations, while he remained a staunch defender of the old order. Another view holds that he suppressed national self-determination and liberalism, infringed civil liberties through a police state, and that the 1848 revolutions exposed the obsolescence of his order, which collapsed soon after his fall because it rested on personal skill rather than institutions.

supporter.zh: 梅特涅被誉为19世纪欧洲最杰出的外交家之一，他通过'欧洲协调'机制成功维护了欧洲近一个世纪的和平与稳定。他敏锐地认识到民族主义的潜在危险，并试图通过大国合作来预防大规模冲突。梅特涅的外交智慧和政治远见使他能够在复杂的国际环境中为奥地利帝国争取最大利益，同时保持欧洲力量的平衡。他建立的维也纳体系为欧洲提供了相对稳定的政治框架，为19世纪大部分时间的经济发展创造了条件。
supporter.en: Metternich is regarded as one of the most outstanding diplomats of 19th-century Europe, successfully maintaining nearly a century of peace and stability through the 'European Concert' mechanism. He keenly recognized the potential dangers of nationalism and attempted to prevent large-scale conflicts through great power cooperation. Metternich's diplomatic wisdom and political foresight enabled him to maximize Austria's interests in the complex international environment while maintaining the balance of power in Europe. The Vienna system he established provided a relatively stable political framework for Europe, creating conditions for economic development throughout most of the 19th century.

critic.zh: 批评者认为梅特涅是欧洲进步的阻碍者，他顽固地维护旧秩序，压制民族自决和自由主义思潮。他的保守政策延缓了欧洲民主化进程，使许多民族处于被统治地位。梅特涅的警察国家政策侵犯了公民自由，他的外交手段常常被视为不道德和机会主义。1848年革命浪潮表明，他试图维持的秩序已经无法适应时代发展。此外，梅特涅过度依赖个人外交手腕，缺乏制度性安排，导致他下台后其建立的体系迅速瓦解。
critic.en: Critics view Metternich as a阻碍者 of European progress, stubbornly maintaining the old order and suppressing national self-determination and liberal thought. His conservative policies delayed Europe's democratization process, leaving many nations under foreign rule. Metternich's police state policies infringed upon civil liberties, and his diplomatic methods were often seen as immoral and opportunistic. The 1848 revolutionary wave demonstrated that the order he tried to maintain could no longer adapt to the times. Additionally, Metternich过度依赖 personal diplomatic skills rather than institutional arrangements, leading to the rapid collapse of his system after his downfall.

objective.zh: 历史学界普遍认为梅特涅是欧洲从革命时代向稳定过渡时期的关键人物。他既是旧秩序的维护者，也是新型国际关系的构建者。梅特涅的'均势外交'理念对现代国际关系理论产生了深远影响，他的'欧洲协调'概念成为后来国际联盟和联合国的思想先驱。在流行文化中，梅特涅常被描绘为精于算计的外交大师，但也被视为保守顽固的象征。他的复杂性在于他既是启蒙思想的受益者，又是反对激进变革的保守派；既维护君主制，又接受理性治国原则。
objective.en: Historiography generally regards Metternich as a pivotal figure in Europe's transition from revolutionary era to stability. He was both a defender of the old order and a builder of new international relations. Metternich's 'balance of power' diplomacy has had a profound impact on modern international relations theory, and his 'European Concert' concept became an intellectual precursor to later the League of Nations and the United Nations. In popular culture, Metternich is often depicted as a calculating diplomatic master but also as a symbol of conservative stubbornness. His complexity lies in being both a beneficiary of Enlightenment thought and an opponent of radical change; upholding monarchy while accepting principles of rational governance.

self.zh: 当革命的风暴席卷欧洲时，我宁愿看到半个世界沉沦，也不愿看到欧洲秩序崩溃。
self.en: When revolutionary storms swept across Europe, I would rather see half the world perish than see the collapse of European order.
